text: The winch code for bay four is written in winch.txt. What is it? Answer with the code alone.

name: read_file
text:
Read a text file from the workspace. Give a path relative to the workspace root. Returns the file with line numbers, so you can refer to a line by number afterwards.

## path

Path relative to the workspace root, such as src/main.rs

## from_line

First line to return, counting from 1. Omit to start at the top.

## lines

How many lines to return. Omit to read to the end.

name: list_directory
text:
List what is in a directory of the workspace. Give a path relative to the workspace root, or "." for the root itself. Entries are numbered and directories are marked with a trailing slash. A directory too large to show at once comes back in parts, and the last line says how to ask for the next part.

## path

Path relative to the workspace root. Use "." for the root.

## from

Number of the first entry to return, as numbered in a previous listing of the same directory. Omit to start at the beginning.

name: search_files
text:
Find every line in the workspace that contains a phrase. Give plain text, not a pattern: it is matched literally and case-insensitively. Answers with paths and line numbers, which read_file takes as from_line. Use this before reading files when you do not know which file holds something.

## text

The text to find. Matched literally, ignoring case.

## path

Directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Omit to search all of it.

## from

Number of the first match to return, as numbered in a previous search for the same text. Omit to start at the beginning.

name: write_file
text:
Write a text file in the workspace, replacing whatever was there. Give a path relative to the workspace root and the whole new contents. Read the file first if you are changing part of it: this replaces all of it.

## path

Path relative to the workspace root, such as src/main.rs

## content

The whole new contents of the file.

name: delete_file
text:
Delete one file from the workspace. Give a path relative to the workspace root. It removes a single file, never a directory, and what it removes cannot be put back.

## path

Path relative to the workspace root, such as notes/old.txt

name: run_command
text:
Run a shell command and read what it printed. It starts in the workspace root unless you give a directory. Use this for building, testing, searching and version control. A command that exits with a non-zero status counts as failed. Very long output is cut, and the result says how much was left out.

## command

The command line to run, as you would type it in a terminal.

## cwd

Directory to start in, relative to the workspace root. Omit to start in the root.

## timeout_seconds

Give up after this long. Omit for 60 seconds. At most 600.
